minimum_cardinality_contract.status: semantic_design_only_engine_gap; not an executable form_contract bucket
minimum_cardinality_contract.unit: One documented supplied chainring crown occurrence per row. An inseparable 2x assembly can contain two crowns; two copies of a crown remain two occurrences.
preconditions: Both fields resolve by active definition ID in the same template/tenant and contract revision. Neither endpoint is legacy.
The total passes the existing exact number/integer/minimum validator. Invalid metadata fails closed.
Each valid row id denotes an included crown occurrence, not an OEM option, a mounting position or an additional reading of the same occurrence.
Existing row-shape validation owns malformed rows and duplicate ids; do not count malformed documents.
The row table has one-per-occurrence content semantics; no quantity-column summation is part of this minimum.
algorithm: Validate total and table types first. Preserve existing scalar/row_shape conflicts; do not substitute guessed values.

Let N be the exact declared integer total when present. Let R be the number of valid distinct supplied-crown rows currently documented; do not count positions, teeth values, sources, option choices or members.
If N is absent, report total/completeness pending without deriving N from R.
If N=0 and rows are absent, the cardinality relation is consistent. An explicit nonempty table contradicts zero; reuse the current field_applicability owner rather than duplicate that diagnosis.
If N>0 and R>N, emit blocking cardinality conflict on the rows field, naming declared and documented quantities.
If N>0 and R<N (including an absent table), emit nonblocking completeness pending. Do not synthesize rows or delete observations.
If R=N, the count is balanced only. Keep missing cell/source/variant evidence issues and all mechanical-fit checks independent.
Compare exact decimal integers; do not cast a large total through floating point. Renaming/reordering a row or adding another source does not change R.

kit_members_boundary: Do not sum kit_members.quantity in the minimum rule. That table can contain nested sets, monoblocks, variants and independently incomplete observations.
A family token alone does not identify measurement unit or prove that members are disjoint supplied crowns. A member label such as plato does not supply that proof either.

A future reconciliation needs confirmed type, included status, exact variant, quantity unit and parent/child/disjoint scope plus stable occurrence links. Parent crankset and its included crowns must not be counted twice.
If those scopes are absent, remain pending; do not infer zero from no matching member rows and do not deduce crown count from a crankset/bicycle member.
drivetrain_kit has no chainring_teeth_rows endpoint in this stage. Do not attach the crankset relation to a nonexistent field or implicitly require bielas.
activation_gates: New metadata must fail closed on old clients; an ignored unknown bucket is not sufficient. Preserve already published metadata versions.
Implement equivalent Dart, SQL draft/write/reference projection and schema-publication checks on the final merged snapshot.
Total and rows must be validated from the same revision; endpoint metadata changes require guarded publication and concurrency tests, not separate reads.
Preserve omitted rows/cells/sources during fill merge, then evaluate cardinality on the merged result.
No auto-fill, source verification, mechanical approval or identity reassignment follows from a balanced count.
